body:
I can confirm this on 4.5.beta1 (using Jolt).

What's the best way to fix this?

- When toggling a vertex, also toggle vertices at the same position.
- Only show a gizmo per actual vertex unique position in the first place. Toggling this gizmo will toggle vertices at the same position automaticvally.
  - This ensures we don't draw overlapping gizmos, which is faster. However, how do we ensure the mapping between the gizmos you see and what the PhysicsServer expects remains correct?

Both approaches will require looping through all vertices to determine unique positions, which could be slow for meshes with thousands of vertices or more.

Personally I think the best fix is to only draw 1 gizmo per physics vertex, by having SoftBody3D keep track of the render vertex <-> physics vertex mapping.

Currently this mapping is done in the physics server, but I think it should be done in the SoftBody3D code instead, and we should only tell the physics server about the actual physics vertices, and not the full list of render vertices.  This is inline with my suggestions in godotengine/godot-proposals#12670 for improving the PhysicsServer3D APIs.

In the short term this would require having 2 copies of this mapping, which is slightly unfortunate (adding a copy in SoftBody3D, in addition to the data tracked in the physics server).  For this particular gizmo UI problem we could track this extra copy of the map only when running in the editor.  However, having this vertex mapping available in SoftBody3D would also help with some other issues, like improving the shading behavior by moving render normal calculation into SoftBody3D (instead of having the physics servers doing this rendering logic).
